claim: Common mitigation strategies for forgetting in LLM post-training primarily expose a stability–plasticity trade-off rather than a universal solution.
falsifier: For a given LLM and post-training task, apply a candidate mitigation strategy and measure both retention of pre-training capabilities (stability) and acquisition of new capabilities (plasticity); the claim predicts that improvements in plasticity will be accompanied by degradation in stability, and no strategy eliminates this trade-off.

conditions: Post-training setting with forgetting mitigation applied
Evaluation across multiple model families and domains
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported mitigation strategies, model families, and domains; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Mitigation strategies–Trade-off between stability boundary
